annotations.keyFindings: Across 31 studies, visits fell after enrolment, but trials found smaller reductions (median 12 percent); only 6 studies reported mortality or ICU admission.
Among 8,900 frequent attenders, 12-month death or ICU admission affected 6.0 percent.
annotations.limitations: Another region; outcome coding from linked data.

annotations.keyFindings: With 64 cases and four matched controls each, enrolment had an odds ratio of 0.62 (0.38 to 1.01) for death or ICU admission.
annotations.limitations: Single site; few cases; enrolment favoured social needs.

annotations.keyFindings: Enrolled patients had more prior visits and complexity; unadjusted, enrolment appeared to double death risk, and the association reversed after adjustment.
Abstractors agreed on enrolment date (kappa 0.81) but only moderately on contact counts (0.58); a file took 44 minutes.
Caseloads ranged from 35 to 80 per case manager and enrolment took 3 weeks at tertiary against 9 weeks at community departments.
Incidence density sampling recovered the rate ratio; sampling from end-of-follow-up survivors overstated protection by up to 30 percent.

claims.text: A single-site matched case-control study with 64 cases found an odds ratio of 0.62 for death or ICU admission with case management enrolment, with an interval that included 1.
claims.passage: Case management enrolment before the index date was less common among cases (odds ratio 0.62, 95 percent CI 0.38 to 1.01)
claims.interpretation: A planning value; a single site gave an imprecise estimate.

claims.text: Without adjustment for prior visits and comorbidity, case management enrolment appeared to double the risk of death; after adjustment the association reversed.
claims.passage: Without adjustment for these factors, enrolment appeared to double the risk of death; after adjustment for prior visit count and a comorbidity index, the association reversed.
claims.interpretation: Match or adjust on prior utilisation and comorbidity.

synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. Case management reduces visits less than before-after studies suggest, and hard outcomes are rarely evaluated. One single-site case-control study found a protective but imprecise association with death or ICU admission. Confounding by indication can reverse the apparent effect unless prior utilisation and comorbidity are handled, exposure is best measured as enrolment date, controls must be sampled by incidence density, and programme intensity differs between tertiary and community sites. Death or ICU admission affects about 6 percent of frequent attenders a year.
gradeRationale: One imprecise case-control study on the outcome of interest and supporting methods evidence; low certainty for any effect on death or ICU admission.
summary: Seven retrieved records appraised; six claims with passages; certainty low.
